title: How Much Fiber in Lentils? 15.6g per Cup
description: Lentils: about 15.6 g of fiber per 1 cup, cooked (56% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in lentils?

answer.note: USDA FoodData Central, Lentils, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt

intro: Lentils rank #3 of 10 beans and legumes on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in lentils by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in lentils?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists lentils, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt at 7.9 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 cup, cooked; 198 g) therefore has about 15.6 g of fiber and 230 calories. That is 56% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 63% of a 25 g day and 41% of a 38 g day.

Lentils cook in 20–30 minutes without soaking, which makes them the most practical legume for weeknight cooking. A cooked cup supplies fiber in the same league as black and pinto beans, with a softer texture that blends into soups, dals, and sauces.

sections.heading: Dry vs cooked lentils: log the right one
paragraphs: Lentils roughly double to triple in volume as they cook, so a 1/4 cup of dry lentils becomes well over half a cup cooked. If you measure before cooking, log the dry amount; if you scoop from the pot, log cooked. Mixing the two is the most common logging mistake.

Red lentils break down into a purée, while green and brown lentils hold their shape. USDA’s generic cooked-lentil row covers both for logging purposes; if you use a packaged product, its label is the better reference.

sections.heading: How lentils compare with other beans and legumes
paragraphs: Of the 10 beans and legumes on this site, lentils rank #3 for fiber per typical serving and #3 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 6.8 g of fiber per 100 calories, a high ratio: you get a lot of fiber for the calories.

Close neighbors by serving: [pinto beans](/fiber-in-pinto-beans) at 15.4 g (1 cup, cooked); [split peas](/fiber-in-split-peas) at 16.3 g (1 cup, cooked); [black beans](/fiber-in-black-beans) at 15 g (1 cup, cooked). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), lentils are #15 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding lentils to your day
paragraphs: A cup of lentil soup made with plenty of lentils, or half a cup of dal with rice, is an easy weekday add. Lentils also stretch ground meat in tacos and bolognese without changing the dish much.

Example: 1 cup lentils, 1 cup brown rice, 1 cup spinach. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 19.5 g of fiber, with 15.6 g from the lentils. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of lentils?
faqs.a: 7.9 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Lentils, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in lentils (1/2 cup, cooked)?
faqs.a: About 7.8 g, for 99 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.

faqs.q: Are red lentils lower in fiber than green lentils?
faqs.a: Red lentils are usually sold split and hulled, which removes some of the outer seed coat, so they can be somewhat lower in fiber than whole green or brown lentils. Check the package label for the variety you buy.

faqs.q: Is lentil soup a good source of fiber?
faqs.a: It depends on how many lentils are in the bowl. A typical canned or restaurant lentil soup is much thinner than plain cooked lentils, so expect a fraction of 15.6 g per cup. Log homemade soup by the lentils you put in the pot divided by servings.
